tools.name: claim_commit
tools.description:
Commit a claim for an autonomous run and adjudicate it over its ALREADY-GATHERED evidence.

    Call this before your run's FIRST gated external-compute dispatch. It runs the Society
    conductor's adjudication (no new compute) over ``evidence_payload_path`` — a scorer payload JSON
    of shape ``{"score": <n>, "payload": {...}}`` whose ``payload`` should carry the raw-array
    ``probe_inputs`` channel for each required deterministic falsifier — and writes the verdict under
    ``{run_dir}/society``. After it succeeds, pass the same ``run_dir`` to ``slurm_submit`` and VB-3
    gates automatically.

    Identify the run by ``run_id`` (resolved to its dir) or an explicit ``run_dir``. ``claim_id``
    defaults to ``claim_<run>``. ``required_falsifiers`` is a list of gate names (e.g. ``confound``,
    ``permutation_null``); omit it to require the committed HARD self-falsifier axes. The scope
    fields (``population`` / ``modality`` / ``datasets`` / ``workflow_family``) bound the claim.
    ``editorial_mode`` selects role-local enforcement: ``off`` preserves the legacy path,
    ``contested`` convenes roles only for a contested claim, and ``every_claim`` requires a typed
    panel on every adjudicable claim. When ``BR_SOCIETY_EDITORIAL_MODE`` sets a server policy, a
    caller may strengthen but cannot weaken it. Required panel failures are sealed as
    ``panel_incomplete`` and returned through ``editorial_enforcement_complete`` /
    ``editorial_panel_states``; they are never reported as completed enforcement.
    A concurrent attempt for the same run returns ``code=ADJUDICATION_IN_PROGRESS`` with
    ``retryable=true`` instead of interleaving terminal artifacts.

    Gated by ``BR_VB_ADJUDICATE_AUTONOMOUS``: with the flag OFF this is an explicit no-op
    (``adjudicated=False, skipped=True``) — nothing is adjudicated or written.

    Once adjudicated, the verdict also carries the Phase-5 promotion-gate result over this SAME
    ``run_dir`` (``promotion_gate_refusal`` / ``promotion_blocked``) — the same gate the daemon
    path applies, opt-in via ``BR_VB_PROMOTION_GATE`` (default off).

tools.name: neuroclaim_compile
tools.description:
Compile one neuroscience claim into a transparent, gated verdict (not RAG).

    Returns a re-runnable report instead of a summary. Two honesty levels are never
    blurred: a structural failure (e.g. an EEG dataset fed to an fMRI GLM, when a
    ``plan`` is supplied) yields the crisp ``ill_typed`` status and SHORT-CIRCUITS;
    otherwise a soft evidential verdict is produced and a MANDATORY sensitivity sweep
    (lenient vs conservative evidence bar) flags it threshold-fragile if it does not
    survive. Uncertainty is a NAMED VECTOR — extraction confidence is reported but
    never folded into the scientific association strength — and the two big
    neuroimaging mapping uncertainties (coordinate->region, task->ontology) surface
    as explicit missing premises ("sorries").

    Args:
        claim_text: the natural-language claim to gate.
        population/modality/datasets/workflow_family: the scope it is asserted within.
        plan: optional analysis-plan dict; when present it is typechecked (a dict is
            coerced like ``pipeline_plan_validate``), and an error/critical finding
            makes the claim ``ill_typed`` without consulting the evidence layer.
        run_id: optional run to bind the verdict to.
        backend: evidence backend name (``kg_verify`` default; ``neurolang`` falls
            back when unavailable). Defaults to ``BR_NEUROCLAIM_BACKEND`` / kg_verify.
        extraction_confidence: caller's extractor confidence — recorded as its own
            uncertainty dim, never folded into the association probability.
        run_sensitivity: when False the verdict ships with a loud "robustness
            unknown" caveat instead of a sensitivity result (and avoids a 2nd KG call).
        strictness: evidence bar for the reported verdict — ``lenient`` /
            ``balanced`` / ``conservative`` (default lenient). Two fast calls
            (``lenient`` then ``conservative``, both with ``run_sensitivity=False``)
            reproduce the sweep's threshold-fragility check without the 2nd blocking
            verify — useful when the full sweep is close to an interactive timeout.

    Returns:
        ``{"ok": True, ...report fields...}`` or ``{"ok": False, "error": ...}``.

tools.name: neuroclaim_compile_nsquall
tools.description:
Compile a claim WRITTEN IN NSQUALL — the surface language — into the gated report. Same kernel as ``neuroclaim_compile``, but the claim is authored in NSQUALL, which carries what the structured tool cannot: a MODAL operator, a task CONTRAST, and the PIPELINE axes a multiverse quantifies over. So the report additionally exposes ``modal_judgment`` / ``modal_discharge`` (a written ``□`` discharged against a real multiverse profile), and the typed ``contrast`` + ``pipeline_choices`` on the AST — letting an agent state and gate a fully *multiverse-quantified* claim in one call. The report keeps two text surfaces distinct: ``claim_text`` is the proposition as authored and remains authoritative for claim identity, modal discharge, and audit fields; ``evidence_claim_text`` is the parser-derived canonical Region relation authorized for backend grounding. If structural checks reach evidence, that text drives every backend; ordered typed subject/object hints additionally bind KG grounding. The actual backend query is frozen into ``reproducible_query``. An ill-typed claim dispatches no backend query. NSQUALL grammar (one claim; the CONTRAST/PIPELINES lines are optional): CLAIM : [ROBUSTLY,|POSSIBLY,|□|◇ ]In , is associated with . CONTRAST > [test=t|z|f]. SCOPE population=

modality= datasets= workflow=. PIPELINES , , .... CONFIRMATORY|EXPLORATORY [allowing ,] [null=]. Args: nsquall: the NSQUALL claim text. multiverse: an optional robustness profile (``active_frac`` / ``sign_consistency`` / ``effect_size_stability`` / ``n_valid`` / ``binding_status``) the written ``□``/``◇`` is discharged against. Without it a written ``□`` is reported as an unproven premise (fail-closed), never as established. run_id / backend / run_sensitivity / strictness / plan: as in ``neuroclaim_compile``. A malformed NSQUALL claim returns ``{"ok": False, "error": ..., "error_type": "nsquall_syntax"}`` — a typed syntax error, never a raise. Returns ``{"ok": True, ...report fields...}`` or ``{"ok": False, "error": ...}``.

tools.name: neuroclaim_record_start
tools.description:
Start a full auditable claim record as a background run; return a pollable run_id.

    Unlike ``neuroclaim_compile`` (one forward evidence axis), this operationalises a
    *compound* claim end to end in a single call: it seals a commitment
    (commit-before-observe) and then runs up to four evidence axes over the same
    corpus — forward-default, forward-strict (threshold fragility),
    ``specificity_excluding_rivals`` (drops the ``rival_terms``), and
    ``network_coactivation`` (co-activation across ``network_regions``) — composing
    them into one ClaimCard with a matching ``commitment_hash``. Poll ``run_get`` (or
    ``neuroclaim_record_get``); when ``status == "succeeded"`` the full record
    (commitment_card + claim_card + the per-axis evidence_verdicts) is inlined under
    ``result`` together with a separately persisted certificate reference and its
    verification result.  The certificate binds the persisted audit lineage and
    explicitly does not prove empirical truth.

    Pass exactly one authored input form: legacy ``claim_text``, strict ``nsquall``,
    or the canonical ``claim_spec`` mapping returned by ``parse_nsquall``. The typed
    forms carry their subject/object, scope, design, contrast, pipeline choices, and
    modal assertion into the record; their typed region/term determine the backend
    query and a conflicting ``evidence_claim_text`` fails before evidence is observed.
    ``plan`` is the optional executable analysis plan checked before commitment and
    evidence. NSQUALL ``PIPELINES`` choice-axis labels are not treated as plan steps.

    Give the compound claim its operational parts so they are actually queried and not
    silently dropped: ``evidence_claim_text`` is the simple region×term phrase the
    backend grounds (e.g. "the dlPFC is engaged during working memory");
    ``network_regions`` (>=2, e.g. ["dlPFC","IPS"]) drives the co-activation axis;
    ``rival_terms`` (e.g. ["attention"]) drives the specificity axis. An axis whose
    inputs are absent is recorded honestly under ``axes_not_run`` rather than skipped
    silently. ``backend`` defaults to ``BR_NEUROCLAIM_BACKEND`` (nimare in prod);
    ``strictness`` picks the reported bar (lenient/balanced/conservative).

tools.name: neuroprogram_compile
tools.description:
Compile a declarative research PROGRAM: hypothesis + constraints + objectives -> gated report.

    The layer above ``hypothesis_compile_design``: it binds a typed hypothesis (the generator),
    a declared set of review-engine ``constraints`` (rule ids the compiled plan must satisfy),
    the ``claims`` the program intends to license, and ``objectives`` — then LOWERS the program
    onto existing machinery (the Gate-2 design compiler, the plan review rule engine, and the
    V-HRL ceiling composition). It compiles, checks, and ceilings ONE program; it does NOT
    search a design space (the optimizer is deferred by design).

    OBJECTIVE-SAFETY: ``objectives`` may only target validity/robustness/coverage
    (``maximize_robustness`` / ``maximize_coverage`` / ``maximize_reproducibility`` /
    ``maximize_generalization`` / ``minimize_compute_cost``). A magnitude objective
    (``maximize_effect_size`` / ``..._novelty`` / ``..._significance``) is REJECTED with a clear
    reason — optimizing result magnitude over a design space is automated garden-of-forking-paths.

    The report's ``status`` is the strongest claim the program may license: the composed
    reasoning-mode + claim-structure ceiling, lowered to ``unresolved`` when the design abstains
    and to ``ill_typed`` when a constraint blocks. A commitment fingerprint over the
    pre-registration block (hypothesis/scope/claims/constraints/objectives/priors) is returned
    for commit-before-observe. Reads task conditions OFFLINE (no Neo4j); claim evidence
    verification is OPT-IN via ``verify=True`` (Neo4j/NiMARE-bound, ~60s/claim).

    Returns ``{"ok": True, ...report...}`` or ``{"ok": False, "error": ...}``. Never raises.

tools.name: neuroprogram_episode
tools.description:
Autonomously PLAN + COMMIT one NeuroProgram episode: hypothesis -> compiled design ->
    optimized + fingerprint-LOCKED design family, ready to execute (commit-before-observe).

    The agent-facing front door to the autonomous loop. It runs the FAST half synchronously
    (compile_program + optimize_design_family + commit) and returns the committed multiverse to
    run. It does NOT run fitlins: a full multiverse is minutes-to-hours (exceeds an MCP client
    timeout) and needs preprocessed BOLD + an atlas, so EXECUTION is out-of-band — drive the
    committed family with the ``neuroprogram-real-fmri`` skill / ``make_fitlins_multiverse_runner``
    / a SLURM job, then bind the robustness via ``run_neuroprogram_episode``'s synthesis path.

    OBJECTIVE-SAFETY: the design family is fingerprint-locked HERE, before any result is observed;
    objectives may only be validity/robustness/coverage (a magnitude objective is rejected); a
    degenerate prior / unknown declared constraint / no-eligible-family forces ``claim_mode`` to
    exploratory. Offline (no Neo4j, no BOLD). Returns ``{"ok": True, ...}`` or ``{"ok": False, "error"}``.

tools.name: neuroprogram_optimize_design
tools.description:
Search the PRE-REGISTERED design space for the best design family (objective-SAFE).

    Picks WHICH multiverse to commit to running — never which result to keep. Scores candidate
    families on magnitude-free properties only (coverage over the full HRF/high-pass/confound
    axes; an events-free regressor-count efficiency proxy → robustness via across-variant
    stability; declared review-rule satisfaction; compute cost), takes the Pareto front, weights
    by the declared ``objectives``, and FINGERPRINT-LOCKS the winning family (commit-before-observe).

    OBJECTIVE-SAFETY: ``objectives`` may only be validity/robustness/coverage (a magnitude
    objective like ``maximize_effect_size`` is rejected). The fitness never reads any result,
    z-map, or confounds value. A degenerate (near-delta) prior with no pre-data
    ``prior_provenance`` forces ``claim_mode='exploratory'``. Optimization cannot raise a claim
    above its structural ceiling. Offline (no Neo4j, no BOLD); efficiency here is the events-free
    DOF proxy — use the ``neuroprogram-real-fmri`` skill for the events-based design efficiency.

    Returns ``{"ok": True, ...OptimizeResultV1...}`` or ``{"ok": False, "error": ...}``.

tools.name: report_claim_evidence_check
tools.description:
Gate a report's claims through the neuroclaim evidence kernel (opt-in, bounded).

    The evidence-layer companion to ``report_claim_provenance_check``: each claim is
    compiled (evidence verdict + reverse-inference guard + conservative-bar sensitivity
    + named uncertainty), and the result is a "Claim evidence & robustness" summary with
    per-claim status + caveats (threshold-fragile / reverse-inference-capped /
    conflicting / weak); an ill-typed claim blocks in confirmatory mode.

    COST: one backend evidence query per claim, doubled by the sensitivity sweep. The
    kg_verify backend is ~60s/call — set ``BR_NEUROCLAIM_CORPUS`` and pass
    ``backend="nimare"`` for batch use, and/or lower ``max_claims`` / set
    ``run_sensitivity=False``. Bounded by ``max_claims`` (default 6).

    Returns ``{"ok": True, ...gate summary...}`` or ``{"ok": False, "error": ...}``.

tools.name: report_claim_provenance_check
tools.description:
Check report claims are traceable to artifacts/code that actually ran.

    Report-code traceability: builds a provenance index from the run (file
    manifest path+checksum and plan steps) and validates each claim's
    ``artifact_path`` / ``artifact_sha256`` / ``code_ref`` against it. A claim
    fails when it lacks provenance, cites an artifact the run never produced,
    has a checksum that does not match, or names a code ref absent from the
    plan. Returns the unsupported claim ids, a report-ready 'Claims missing
    provenance' section, and (when blocking) a synthetic critical/block
    correctness finding callers can fold into a report verdict. Unsupported
    claims block under ``require_claim_provenance`` or a confirmatory claim mode;
    exploratory runs surface them as a caveat only. This guards against a report
    describing the intended analysis rather than the one that actually ran.

tools.name: society_enqueue_generated_episodes
tools.description:
Generate OOD hypotheses from KG seeds and QUEUE the compilable ones as Society runs.

    The last hop of the autonomous loop: ``sample_ood_hypothesis`` generates two-pole hypotheses
    from ``seed_kg_ids``; each is converted to a typed spec, wrapped in a NeuroProgram, and
    COMPILE-pre-filtered — a spec that abstains (no resolvable contrast) is SKIPPED, never queued.
    Every compilable program is written as a ``queued`` run the autonomous-run daemon then claims,
    runs, and adjudicates. This tool does NOT run the episode (that is the daemon's job).

    Deterministic + idempotent: the run id is derived from the program's commitment fingerprint (no
    clock/random), so re-calling with the same seeds re-queues nothing (already-enqueued runs are
    reported under ``skipped``). The scope fields bound the wrapped claims.

    Owner-scoping: runs are written under a SERVER-OWNED society run root (``BR_SOCIETY_RUN_ROOT`` or
    ``<mcp_run_root>/society_runs``); the caller can NOT supply an arbitrary path, so this cannot
    write into a foreign tree. Returns ``{"ok": True, "enqueued": [...], "skipped": [...],
    "n_generated": N, "n_enqueued": M, "run_root": ...}`` or ``{"ok": False, "error": ...}``.
